nodes.label: Graphify-First Codebase Workflow
nodes.rationale: Scoped graph queries, paths, explanations, and wiki navigation should precede broad raw-source browsing because they return a smaller relevant subgraph.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Maintenance
nodes.rationale: Code changes should be followed by an AST-only graph update, and expected dirty graph outputs should not prevent graph use.

nodes.label: Runtime-Only Execution Path
nodes.rationale: Models, tools, memory, workflows, scheduling, and interactive runs must use one runtime path so execution remains governable and inspectable.

nodes.label: Modular Monolith
nodes.rationale: Explicit module boundaries are valuable immediately, while independent services should wait for measured operational need.

nodes.label: Trace-First Typed Events
nodes.rationale: Every meaningful transition produces a typed persisted event so the platform can explain behavior and preserve failure traces.

nodes.label: Immutable Agent Versions
nodes.rationale: Each run references the exact immutable configuration that produced it so historical traces remain reproducible and explainable.

nodes.label: SQLite-First Persistence
nodes.rationale: SQLite, WAL mode, short transactions, SQLAlchemy repositories, and migrations provide sufficient local durability while preserving a later PostgreSQL adapter path.

nodes.label: Server-Sent Event Delivery
nodes.rationale: SSE fits primarily server-to-client run updates and has simpler reconnection semantics than WebSockets for the initial architecture.

nodes.label: Deterministic Fake Providers and Tools
nodes.rationale: Deterministic adapters make runtime tests independent of network access, cost, and nondeterministic model output.

nodes.label: Next.js Version-Specific Rules
nodes.rationale: The installed Next.js version may differ from training knowledge, so its bundled documentation and deprecation notices must be consulted before coding.

nodes.label: Vertical-Slice Delivery
nodes.rationale: Phases should deliver behavior across API and UI, teach specific concepts, satisfy exit criteria, and avoid starting multiple speculative subsystems.

nodes.label: Scale Only from Evidence
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL, workers, containers, brokers, and vector indexes should be introduced only in response to observed limitations.

nodes.label: Educational AI Systems Engineering
nodes.rationale: Forge exists to reveal why modern agent platforms are designed as they are and to teach the creator to build such systems from first principles.

nodes.label: Build Concepts, Reuse Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Forge should implement agent-runtime concepts itself while relying on proven databases, web frameworks, telemetry, container, and vendor SDK infrastructure.

nodes.label: Forge as an Operating System for Agents
nodes.norm_label: forge as an operating system for agents

nodes.label: Explain Rather Than Hide Complexity
nodes.rationale: Every tool call, planner decision, memory lookup, retry, and workflow transition should be inspectable so the platform itself teaches agent engineering.
